Subject: SigmaHealth MAP kickoff + perf baseline request

Hi Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement and infra teams are aligned on moving forward with Redwood, and we'd like to formalize a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on two parallel tracks: procurement/SLA and a performance evaluation plan so we can close by end of Q2.

For the evaluation track we care most about:
- End-to-end response latency (p50/p95) for 256/512/1024 token responses
- Throughput (requests/sec) under realistic client concurrency (burst and steady-state)
- Token throughput (tokens/sec per GPU) and how it changes with batching and context length
- Memory/KV cache behavior for multi-turn workloads

Can Redwood provide a weekly MAP checkpoint (short status update + meeting notes + action items with owners) that includes the benchmark snapshots above? If possible, please attach an initial MAP template and a suggested cadence.

Security questionnaire is attached to the procurement thread; we will loop that team in separately.

Claire

SigmaHealth

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SigmaHealth MAP kickoff + perf baseline request 

Attaching initial benchmark snapshot and a short summary. Ran on our 8xA100 test pod with the harness linked by Marcus. Repro scripts and raw CSV attached.

Summary (baseline run, model: redwood/gpt-retro-13B-q4):
- Test config: 1k warmup, 5k eval prompts, context length 2048 tokens, batch size 8, fp16, single-GPU worker per process
- Token throughput: 620 tokens/sec per GPU (median across workers)
- End-to-end (512-token responses): p50 = 1.1s, p95 = 2.6s
- Requests/sec (512-token payload): sustained 6.8 rps at batch size 8 (scales linearly with additional GPUs)
- KV cache impact (multi-turn): observed ~12% latency reduction after warm cache for repeated prefixes

Known caveats: harness used synthetic prompts with moderate repetition. We'll run a second pass with Sigma's real prompt set next.

Next tuning steps (week 1):
- Increase batch size to 12 and 16 to measure throughput/latency tradeoffs (Owner: Diego)
- Try Q5/Q4 quantized variants for int8 profiling (Owner: Priya)
- Measure end-to-end latency with streaming + prefix caching enabled (Owner: Diego)

Attachments: benchmark_results_q1.csv

On Tue, Mar 10, 2026 at 09:12 AM Claire Zhang <c.zhang@sigmahealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Diego — this is helpful. Can you also include p99 on the next run and a short note on variability across GPUs?
> 
> Claire

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SigmaHealth MAP kickoff + perf baseline request

Diego — good baseline. A couple of notes from the tuning side:

1) Quantization + Eval plan
- We'll run three quant profiles (fp16 baseline, q4_0, int8 simulated) and pair each with the full quality eval (ROUGE/BLEU where applicable + human spot checks against your prompt set). (Owner: Priya)

2) Batching policy and adaptive batching
- Test static batch sizes (8/12/16) and an adaptive policy that prioritizes latency SLOs for small requests while aggregating larger requests for throughput. (Owner: Diego)

3) KV cache + streaming
- Enable prefix KV caching and compare cold vs warm start latencies. Add streaming to the harness to measure perceived latency for UX. (Owner: Diego)

4) Regression gates
- Rishi and I will own the evaluation suite that must pass before we surface quantized variants to Sigma's prod environment. (Owner: Rishi)

Timeline:
- Week 1 (this week): run initial quant+batch matrix, post results in MAP checkpoint (diego/priya)
- Week 2: run full quality eval on candidate profiles and present tradeoffs in checkpoint

I'll start the quant runs tonight and post a short report by Wed EOD.

Priya
Applied ML, Redwood Inference
